reason:
VALUE AND TRANSFER lens. Four checks against the files, each quantified.
(1) The cited ceiling is the wrong pool. The +0.03-0.046 swap oracle (experiments/l2_daughternet/edge_anatomy/l6_fn_anatomy_report.md s.1/s.3) belongs to annotated nuclei that sit BETWEEN two of our tracks about 9.4 um apart, with matches at 4.4/4.7 um. That report says the fix is a NEW node, not a relink. Variant (a) moves existing nodes by at most r = 1.5-2 um, so it cannot place a node 4.4 um away without taking it off the nucleus it is tracking now. Variant (b) readmits only peaks > 5 um from every node, and the swap-class nucleus has a node at a median 4.4 um, so the exclusion blocks more than half of them. Neither variant reaches the swap oracle.
(2) The addressable pool is small. (a) is 'another V1284 step'. V1284 cut the leak-OOF mean distance by 9.5% (1.686 -> 1.525 um, experiments/coordhead_retrain/out_full_P/report.txt) and was worth +0.007 on x138 public. That is ~0.0007 LB per 1% of distance. 7 um match counts barely react to sub-2 um moves: none 132,366 / public 132,326 / in-sample retrained 132,473, i.e. +0.08% for a 27% distance cut. For (b): 7.37e-6 per FN (1/135,729). Full recovery of the 1,907 a_never FN would be +0.014 in the lab. A realistic 20-25% recovery with correct links gives +0.0028-0.0035 lab and +0.0014-0.0018 public after the 0.5 transfer factor, before node cost. That is also an upper estimate, because x138's own readmit and gap filler already recover part of that pool (the 1,907 were measured on exp39, not x138), and 424 of those nodes have no peak within 10 um at all.
(3) Decisive: the transfer failure mode is already MEASURED on this data, and the proposed gate cannot see it. The team retrained V1284 on Kaggle GT from both embryos. Leak-group OOF showed -19% distance (1.525 -> 1.238 um), but embryo-held-out it was +12.0% WORSE on 44b6 (1.296 -> 1.452 um, z bias -0.54 um) and +0.2% on 6bba, so the kill test failed. Raw peak-to-GT z bias is +0.18 um on 44b6 and +0.82 um on 6bba, so the two annotation conventions differ by ~0.6 um in z, and 6bba holds 85% of GT pairs. The georgexue666 model was trained directly on Kaggle GT, split 128/32 across the SAME two embryos (D1.json). Its D1-val benchmark is therefore the within-embryo, leak-OOF kind of test, the one that said -19% while embryo transfer was -12% worse. On top of that, the 44b6 val clips are overlapping crops of the one dorado recording, so they are not out-of-sample even within the embryo. 'Follows the annotation convention' is the risk itself, because the convention is embryo-specific and the hidden embryos' convention is unknown. At the V1284 slope, a hidden-embryo distance change between +12% worse and +5% better maps to about -0.009 .. +0.004 on the LB. The most likely outcome is ~0, with a real chance of a loss.
(4) External evidence does not beat what we have. The owning team (easonyanyan) is at 0.950, which is +0.003 over the pre-x138 0.947 wall for detector plus 'exposure-bias' edge predictor together, and equal to our exp51. recall@4 um 0.735 at a top-330 cap cannot be compared with the public detector's 0.943 share of matched pairs within 4 um. Pool 2 improves only xy (0.81 um voxels; z stays 1.625 um), while the embryo offsets are largest in z. With LB noise ~0.003 on a single public embryo, a +0.001 effect cannot be detected in one slot.
Expected public gain ~0.000 (range -0.004..+0.003), below the +0.002 bar. Private (71%, other unseen embryos) has the same sign uncertainty; averaging over embryos lowers the variance but not the bias risk.
fix_if_any: Only a narrowed, convention-free version might survive. (i) Drop variant (a) and the swap-oracle claim. (ii) Keep only variant (b) as a DETECTION source: use a precision peak to decide THAT a nucleus exists, but take its coordinates from the public detector's own sub-threshold heatmap (or the V1284 head at that point), so the embryo-specific annotation offset learned by the georgexue model never enters positions. Use only xy agreement (<= 1.6 um) and never its z. (iii) Replace the D1-val distance gate with a convention diagnostic that CAN fail: on D1-val, per embryo, compute mean(precision peak - V1284-refined public peak) in z/y/x. If the two embryos' mean vectors differ by > 0.2 um on any axis (the same WARN threshold as the head kill test), the model has learned an embryo convention, so kill it. (iv) Gate (b) on the x138 lab cache, 6bba and 44b6 separately: J up by >= +0.002 on both, node multiplier change <= +0.3%, and >= 55% of videos improved. Count added nodes against the annotated fraction (6bba ~14%, 44b6 ~1%), not against 'unannotated-region nodes', which sparse GT cannot measure. Even repaired, the realistic public gain is ~+0.001 (a_never readmit x0.5 transfer, on top of x138's own readmit), still below +0.002, so it is only worth a slot if the lab shows >= +0.004 on both embryos.
realistic_public_gain: ~0.000 (range -0.004 to +0.003). Variant (a): sign unknown on an unseen embryo (the head-retrain precedent maps to -0.009..0 at the V1284 slope of ~0.0007 per 1% distance). Variant (b): <= +0.0015 after transfer and before node cost, partly overlapping x138's own readmit. Below +0.002 and below LB noise 0.003.
realistic_private_gain: ~0.000 to -0.002 (guess). Private is 71% on further unseen embryos. The localiser part bakes in the Kaggle-GT (6bba-dominated) convention, which the embryo-held-out test showed is worse on another embryo. The readmit part could be about +0.001 if it adds real nuclei.
critical_path: As proposed: a browser pass on the dataset (licence, model code, D1.json) on 25-26 Sep. Friend A runs pool-2 inference on the 32 D1-val movies plus the gate, then an x138 lab-cache replay on 26 Sep, then agent build, a Kaggle dummy run (~1 GPU-h, vitalii after the 26 Sep 00:00 reset), commit ~27 Sep 00:05, submit ~01:00, scored ~27 Sep 08:00-11:00 UTC. Blocking unknowns: model code may be missing (the dataset is 46 MB of weights; no GitHub mirror found), friend A's availability is uncertain, and the extra pool-2 UNet pass lengthens the hidden run toward the runtime guard and the 12 h limit. Even if it is scored on time, a <= +0.001 effect is not distinguishable from LB noise 0.003.
